Owen Ford is a tall, broad-shouldered man with thick brown hair. He possesses a finely-cut nose and chin, complimented by large, brilliant dark-gray eyes.

## History

Owen Ford, a newspaper man and short story writer who suffered a bad spell of typhoid, was ordered to the sea by his doctor to recover his health. Arriving at [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds), he arranged to board with [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) and reconnected with the area through his grandfather, [John Selwyn](../character/john-selwyn.md), while aspiring to write a great novel. He met Captain Jim, became enthralled by the old man's life experiences, and spent the summer working intensely at the lighthouse to write a manuscript combining Captain Jim's life story with the tale of lost [Margaret](../character/margaret.md). During his stay, Owen fell deeply in love with [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md), but he departed at the end of the summer in agony over leaving her bound to her tragic marriage. Unaware that [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) secretly harbored feelings for him, he later learned that her circumstances had changed when her husband's true identity was revealed. Owen returned to [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) for a visit, attempted to reconnect with [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md), and ultimately confessed his love to her in the garden. After [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) reciprocated his feelings and they sealed their commitment, they celebrated their future together alongside their friends and Captain Jim shortly before the old man's death.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P1](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0001), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P2](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0002), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P4](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0004), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P6](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0006), +248 more_

## Quotes

> "Mrs. Blythe, this is a wonderful book—absolutely wonderful. If I could take it and use the material for a book I feel certain I could make the novel of the year out of it. Do you suppose Captain Jim would let me do it?"
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000)

> “We’ll collaborate,” cried Owen delightedly. “You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work.”
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)

> “I have a good deal to do to it yet—revising and pruning and so forth,” he said, “but in the main it’s done. I wrote the last sentence this morning. If I can find a publisher for it it will probably be out next summer or fall.”
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P19](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0019)

> "Yes,—he’s mentally deficient, or something of the sort, isn’t he? But she said nothing about Mrs. Moore, and I supposed she’d be the usual hustling country housewife who takes in boarders to earn an honest penny."
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P30](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0030)

> "Oh, I won’t mind him. I don’t suppose I’ll be much in the house anyhow, except for meals. But what a shame it all is! Her life must be a hard one."
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P32](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0032)

## Relationships

### [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/leslie-moore--owen-ford.md)

Owen first met [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) when he arrived at [Four Winds Harbor](../codex/places.md#four-winds-harbor) to board at her home for the summer, where he was immediately struck by her beauty. Over the course of his stay, the two grew close while spending leisure time together alongside their mutual friends, leading to a romantic interest and mutual love between them. Although [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) initially distresses over what she believes is unrequited love, Owen harbours strong feelings for her, with local friends observing his profound effect on her life.

- Romantically involved with — mutual love and courtship  <sub>[v4 CHAPTER 26 OWEN FORD’S CONFESSION P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 CHAPTER 28 ODDS AND ENDS P24](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0024), [v4 CHAPTER 32 MISS CORNELIA DISCUSSES THE AFFAIR P18](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0018), +3 more</sub>

### [Uncle Jim](../character/uncle-jim.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/owen-ford--uncle-jim.md)

After [Anne](../character/anne.md) introduces Owen to Captain Jim at [Four Winds Point](../codex/places.md#four-winds-point), Owen becomes enthralled by the old man's sea tales and borrows his personal life-book. Recognizing the power of these memories, Owen collaborates with Captain Jim by setting up a workspace at the lighthouse to write a book combining Captain Jim's life story with the tale of lost [Margaret](../character/margaret.md). Their partnership as friends and comrades proves successful, culminating in the completed manuscript securing publication.

- Comrade of — collaborators on the book  <sub>[v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 CHAPTER 39 CAPTAIN JIM CROSSES THE BAR P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005)</sub>
- Friend of — collaborator writing his life-book  <sub>[v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)</sub>
